exposure: type of caesarean section (elective vs. emergency)
cohort: The study included 300 pregnant patients undergoing caesarean section with spinal anaesthesia at Muhimbili National Hospital, excluding those with sedation, anti-hypertensive use, pregnancy-induced hypertension, modified Bromage score, or combination anaesthesia.
finding: Hypotension occurred in 56.7% of patients undergoing caesarean section with spinal anaesthesia, with risk factors including preload <10 mL/kg, higher sensory block levels, and absence of wedge positioning.
